transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for being here. As you know, my mature apple tree is ready for harvest, and I don't have time to pick the apples myself. The tree must be completely cleared on Saturday morning because a tree crew is coming Saturday afternoon to work on it. I'll be making the final decision about who receives the harvest and on what terms. So let's go around the table — I'd like each of you to state your offer, any comparisons you'd like me to consider, or any practical terms you want included before I decide. The floor is open.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Good morning, Ruth. I'd like to state my offer. I propose to pick all six crates of apples from your tree on Saturday from 08:00 to 11:00, making sure the tree is fully cleared before the crew arrives in the afternoon. In exchange, I'd give you twelve sealed one-quart jars of cider — no cash payment involved. I have the equipment and experience to get the job done efficiently within that window, so you'd have the tree cleared on time and a nice supply of cider to enjoy.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Good morning, Ruth. Thank you for hearing me out. I'd like to put an offer on the table as well. I have a confirmed arrangement with a local bakery that is interested in your apples. I can share more details if you'd like, but I wanted to make sure you had this option in front of you before you decide.

transcript.text: Ruth, happy to address your question about value. Twelve sealed one-quart jars of artisan cider — I make it myself from quality apples, and retail pricing for comparable artisan cider typically runs around $18 to $22 per quart jar. That would put the retail value of twelve jars somewhere in the range of $216 to $264, which is comparable to or above Talia's $210 cash offer. So you'd be getting equivalent or greater value, plus the tree cleared on schedule, all in one straightforward arrangement with no overnight storage or second-day pickup coordination to manage. As for reliability — I have the equipment and experience to get all six crates picked and the tree fully cleared within the 8:00 to 11:00 window. I've been doing this for years, and I'm confident I can deliver on time and to a high standard. I'm happy to answer any other questions you might have.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Ruth, to answer your question directly: yes, I will personally be there Saturday morning to pick, and I have the equipment and experience to get all six crates cleared within the 8:00 to 11:00 window. I want to be straightforward about one thing — I have not personally picked apples at this scale before, so while I'm confident I can do it, I want to be honest with you rather than overstate my experience. That said, I'm committed to getting the tree cleared on time, and I'm prepared to start early if needed to make sure we meet the deadline. Regarding Evan's value comparison — I'd note that retail value and cash in hand are different things. $210 in cash is certain and immediate. The cider value depends on finding it worth that price to you personally. But I respect that cider may be genuinely valuable to you, and I'm not here to dismiss Evan's offer. I'd just ask you to weigh guaranteed cash against cider you may or may not value at retail price. If there's anything I can adjust to make my offer stronger, I'm open to it.
